north_star: A Telegram instruction is enough for a trusted agent to safely diagnose, configure, repair, and verify a self-hosted *arr media stack.
wedge: An agent-first operational contract and control plane over existing *arr APIs, not another dashboard or a replacement for Sonarr and Radarr.
target_user: Self-hosters who want an agent to operate their media automation stack without manual cross-application configuration.
core_promise: Point an agent at this repository, describe the desired outcome, and receive a verified result or an explicit blocker.
product_principles: Telegram is the human interface; deterministic CLI and APIs are the agent interface.
Plan before apply, verify after mutation, and fail closed when evidence is missing.
Keep private deployment state, credentials, media metadata, and runtime artifacts outside Git.
non_goals: Reimplement Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, download clients, or media servers.
Ship a generic dashboard before the operational control plane is proven.
Commit real household configuration, API keys, media libraries, download history, or host inventories.
success_metrics: A fresh clone explains the product and passes all local gates without private infrastructure.
An agent can discover the next task and its acceptance criteria entirely from repo-local .go state.
Future adapters can prove doctor, plan, apply, rollback, and verify behavior against synthetic fixtures.
